__4 N. of a Ṛṣi, the husband of Aditi and Diti, and thus the father both of gods and demons, (so called because he drank कश्य ‘liquor’; cf. कश्यपस्तस्य पुत्रोऽभूत कश्यपानात् स कश्यपः । [[Mārk. P.]]) [He was the son of Marīchi, the son of Brahmā. He bears a very important share in the work of creation. According to Māhabhārata [Page0551-1] and other accounts, he married Aditi and 12 other daughters of Dakṣa, and begot on Aditi the twelve Ādityas. By his other twelve wives he had a numerous and very diversified progeny: serpents, reptiles, birds, demons, nymphs of the lunar constellation. He was thus the father of gods, demons, men, beasts, birds and reptiles -- in fact of all living beings. He is therefore often called Prajāpati]. 
-Comp.
